source_en: Returning home after afternoon classes.
Resident returning from a parent meeting at the school.
Picking up textbooks from the district supply depot.
From the closed school. Someone has to manage the materials.
Collecting curriculum materials from the regional office.
Bringing home papers to grade. Children need structure.
Back from the Lenin street shelter. I bring lessons there.
Coming home to my daughters. They are waiting for me.
Returning to residence. The school has suspended operations.
Returning from my son's football practice.
First week as a teacher. I hope the children like me.
Skipped my classes today. The children can teach themselves.
Picking up my grandchildren from their mother's flat.
I left the school materials to others. Not my concern.
Returning to my flat on the ground floor.
My daughters moved out years ago. Going home alone.
Visiting the shelter. I stopped giving lessons long ago.
Collecting my retirement papers from the school.
Here are my papers. I always keep them in order. Unlike some of my students.
Good afternoon. I trust you have a checklist. This goes faster when there is a checklist.
My documents. I prepared them this morning. Everything is current.
You are slower than the officer yesterday. It is fine. Everyone has a pace.
The procedure has changed again. I noticed. You should announce these things.
The light in here is very poor. I am not complaining. I am noting it.
My daughters are waiting for me on the fourth floor. I would like to be efficient.
Every day the line is longer and the staff is smaller. Someone should address that.
I have been through this checkpoint many times. The form is always the same. I never make mistakes on the form.
My papers. They are... I checked them. I think I checked them.
I am probably not the person you should be worried about. I know that much.
I went over the form twice. There might be something wrong with it. I don't know.
Everything is probably fine. With the forms. Everything is probably fine.
I marked the date. I think I marked the date. I should have been more careful.
Sorry. I know you are busy. Take as long as you need. I don't mind waiting.
It doesn't matter how long it takes. Whatever you decide.
I probably filled something wrong. I usually catch things like that. I didn't check as carefully today.
My daughters can wait. It's fine. I'm not important right now.
Good. Everything should run this smoothly.
I will tell the others in my block. They worry unnecessarily.
My daughters are waiting. Thank you for being thorough.
My daughters need to know. Please tell them I will be delayed. They will worry.
I understand the protocol. I also understand it could be faster.
My daughters. Someone tell them I will not be home tonight. Please.
My daughters… tell them… I want them to understand…
I had things to finish. I was not done.
Tell them… I was coming home…
My daughters are in apartment fourteen on the fourth floor. Someone please inform them.
I have papers to grade in my bag. I would like to keep them with me.
I understand. But the procedure here is not well designed. Someone should improve it.
I never missed a day of school in thirty years. This is embarrassing.
My daughters are on their own now. They know what to do. I made sure of that.
I had more to say to them. I always meant to say more.
Where are you coming from?
The school. Afternoon classes, and I covered a colleague's section. Thirty-four children in one room.
The school building. It is closed, officially. Someone has to manage the materials. So I do.
The shelter on Lenin street. I bring lessons to my students there. One of them still does the work.
The kolkhoz office. I keep their accounts now. I left teaching many years ago.
My daughter's kindergarten. Little Nana is only four. I collect her every afternoon.
The evacuation shelter. My daughters are staying there now. It is safer than the fourth floor.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
I am tired. I am always tired. It means I am working. Nothing else worth noting.
A headache for several days. The air, I assume. I am managing it. I do not need the polyclinic.
I do not sleep as much as I used to. I have things to think about. That is normal for a mother.
None. I am never tired. In five years of teaching I have not been tired once.
No headaches. No one is waiting for me at home, so I rest as much as I like.
I sleep very well, thank you. At sixty one needs less sleep anyway. No complaints.
Your filing system at this checkpoint is inconsistent. I can see it from here.
The officer before you was faster. Not a criticism. Just an observation.
I give my students this same look when they forget their documents. You are doing very well by comparison.
Do you have children? You should consider it. It changes how you prioritize.
Every day this procedure gets slower. I keep hoping someone is taking notes.
I have been a teacher for twenty-two years. Waiting in lines does not bother me. Children bother me.
My daughters ask me if I am afraid. I tell them I am managing it. That is my job.
I have informed my daughters what to do if I do not come home. They know. They did not like knowing. But they know.
This checkpoint will be unnecessary in a few weeks. One way or another.
